  "text": "The boat grounded with a sound like a chair dragged across a kitchen floor.

Elias did not offer his hand. Mara stepped into the shallows and felt mud enter her shoes.

“You’re late,” he said.

She almost laughed. He had said that once when she came home from market, though he had sent her back for something he’d forgotten. Was this a memory, too? She could no longer trust herself to know.

“I didn’t know you were waiting.”

“Neither did I.”

Behind her, the ferryman rested his pole across the boat. He seemed occupied with a knot in the wood.

Mara had prepared an apology so often that its first words rose without her permission. She pressed her lips together.

Elias glanced at her wet shoes.

“There’s a stone you can sit on.”

“Will you sit with me?”

“I’ve been sitting.”

He walked along the bank. After a moment she followed, carrying all the things she had meant to say. The children’s names seemed suddenly too large to introduce. Even their father’s death required a beginning she could not find.

“Did you take it?” she asked.

He stopped.

“The crust. Off my plate.”

“What?”

“When we were little.”

“How should I remember?”

Disappointment moved through her, sharp and embarrassing. She had brought him this small thing as carefully as a gift.

Then he bent, picked a burr from his trouser leg, and flicked it toward the river.

“You used to leave them,” he said.

“I liked saving them for last.”

“You never told me.”

“I thought you knew.”

He looked at her then, not kindly, not unkindly.

“Well,” he said. “I didn’t.”"
